name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
description: An off-highway motor vehicle that travels on no more than two tires, with a seat the rider straddles and handlebar steering, used only off the highway and not equipped for it, such as an off-road e-moto. Defined and regulated by the Off-Highway Motor Vehicle Act, NMSA 1978 §66-3-1001 et seq.
restrictions: No more than two tires, a seat the rider straddles and handlebar steering; used exclusively off the highway and not legally equipped for it
Can't be registered as street legal
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Division on a two-year cycle, with an "OH" sticker on the rear; nonresidents need a nonresident permit
Riders under 18 must wear a securely fastened safety helmet and eye protection, and must hold an off-highway motor vehicle safety permit from a certified course

Riders 10 to 17 must be visually supervised by a parent, guardian or licensed adult, unless they're 13 or older with a motorcycle license or 15 or older with a driver's license or permit, plus a safety permit
Riders under 10 may ride only an age-appropriate, size-fit vehicle under a parent's, guardian's or certified instructor's supervision
Must have a spark arrester and be no louder than 96 decibels
Kept to 10 mph within 200 feet of an occupied dwelling, pedestrians or animals
Local paved-road authorization covers only all-terrain and recreational off-highway vehicles, not off-highway motorcycles
